diagnostic: Same-run bounded timing trace correlating V4L2 DQBUF syscalls, FFmpeg showinfo source PTS, FFmpeg raw output frame-byte boundaries, and Python full-frame read completion. Raw syscall arguments only; no frame payload captured or saved.
interpretation: V4L2 DQBUF and source PTS cadence are regular after startup; FFmpeg output write-boundary and Python read-completion cadence both contain >60ms gaps and closely match. The timing evidence localizes the observed jitter after V4L2 buffer dequeue and before raw pipe delivery, but does not distinguish FFmpeg decode/output pacing from FFmpeg-thread host scheduling or pipe backpressure. The DQBUF raw trace omits V4L2 buffer sequence fields, so exact dequeue-to-output frame identity is not asserted.
limitations: 600-frame traced sample only; strict AC-4 still requires the five-minute acceptance capture after a proven fix.
strace changes scheduling; compare distributions cautiously.
The V4L2 PTS is start-of-exposure (SOE); it is not timestampEof.
source_semantics: showinfo PTS timebase 1/1000000 maps to monotonic clock per prior same-device validation; V4L2 timestamp source is ts-src-soe, not EOF. DQBUF is kernel buffer delivery to FFmpeg; Python time is immediately after full raw NV12 read. No source timestamp is relabeled as EOF.
